issues.legal_issue: A lease granting alternative purposes of planting a grove and erecting buildings is not exclusively a lease for erecting buildings when no building has been constructed.
material_facts: The lease permitted planting a grove, erecting buildings, and digging wells.
No building had been constructed on the land.
The lessees claimed that their predecessor had planted a grove.
issues.conclusion: The lease could not be classified exclusively as a building lease; if a qualifying grove had been planted and was being used as a grove on the relevant date, the land could fall within the provision concerning grove land.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of the lease and the land’s actual use determine its classification. The Court distinguished land potentially covered as grove land from land held under a building lease.

predicates.lease_permits_multiple_purposes: The lease permits the land to be used for more than one purpose, including planting a grove and erecting buildings.
predicates.buildings_not_constructed: No building has been constructed on the leased land.

issues.definition: When a lease permits multiple purposes and no building has been constructed, the lease is not exclusively a building lease.

issues.legal_issue: A provision including land held on a lease for erecting buildings within an agricultural area is limited to land used for agricultural purposes and, so construed, is protected from the asserted constitutional challenge.
material_facts: The law’s stated purpose was abolition of the zamindari system in agricultural areas and introduction of land reforms.
Other categories in the definition of agricultural area concerned land used for crops, groves, or pasture, and the definition excluded certain land occupied by buildings.
Related provisions conferred rights on lessees of land in an agricultural area and addressed its use for erecting buildings.
The provision was challenged as unrelated to agricultural reform and as violating constitutional protections.
issues.conclusion: The provision applies only to land in an agricultural area used for agricultural purposes; on that construction it is connected with agricultural reform and is protected by Article 31A from the asserted challenges under Articles 14, 19, and 31.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the provision in its statutory context and in light of the Act’s purpose, including the relationship between sections 2(1)(d), 17(1)(b), and 19(j), and the definition of land under the U.P. Tenancy Act, 1939. It agreed with the result in Durga Prasad v. Board of Revenue, U.P., Allahabad, A.I.R. 1970 All. 159, although for different reasons. On this limited construction, the provision is connected with agricultural reform and receives the protection of Article 31A of the Constitution.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_proceeding: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law provision in a proceeding concerning land reform.
predicates.provision_limited_to_agricultural_use: The provision, properly construed, applies only to land used for agricultural purposes.

issues.definition: In a constitutional challenge to a land-reform provision, a provision limited to land used for agricultural purposes is protected from the asserted constitutional challenge.

issues.legal_issue: A vesting notification cannot stand when the available evidence does not establish that the land qualified as an agricultural area on the relevant date, and the land’s status must be determined afresh.
material_facts: The land was alleged to form part of a residential property and not to be agricultural land.
The government’s response did not address the identified plot because it proceeded on a mistaken understanding of the plot’s number.
A commissioner reported that part of the plot was vacant and that trees on the land were scattered; the report did not establish that the plot was a grove under the applicable definition.
The record did not permit a concluded finding that the land was an agricultural area or was being used for horticulture on the relevant date.
A notification declaring the land vested in the State had been issued.
issues.conclusion: The Court quashed the notification as to the land and directed a fresh determination. A new notification could be issued only if the inquiry established that the land was an agricultural area and was being used for agriculture or horticulture on the relevant date.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Act’s definition of agricultural area, read with its purpose and the relevant provisions, only qualifying agricultural land could be acquired. Whether the land met that definition had to be determined by the appropriate authority on the evidence; the existing record did not establish that it did.

predicates.challenge_to_vesting_notification: A party challenges a notification that declares land vested in the State under an agricultural land-reform scheme.
predicates.agricultural_status_not_established: The available evidence does not establish that the land qualified as agricultural land and was being used for agriculture or horticulture on the relevant date.

issues.definition: When a vesting notification is challenged and the evidence does not establish the land’s agricultural status, the notification must be quashed pending a fresh classification.

issues.legal_issue: Suits and appeals cannot remain abated on the basis of a vesting notification that has been quashed while the land’s qualification as an agricultural area remains unresolved.
material_facts: The High Court had abated pending appeals and the suits from which they arose under the applicable rules after a vesting notification was issued.
The Supreme Court quashed that notification and directed a fresh inquiry into whether the land was an agricultural area.
The suits and appeals concerned possession of the land and specific performance of an agreement to re-let it.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the orders abating the suits and appeals and directed that they be restored. The appeals were to be decided on their merits if the land was found not to be an agricultural area; if it was found to be an agricultural area and a notification was issued, they were to be disposed of in accordance with the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 38 and 39 provide for the stay and abatement of specified suits and appeals in the circumstances prescribed by the Act. Where the vesting notification underlying an abatement is quashed and the land’s status remains to be determined, the abatement orders cannot stand; the proceedings must be restored and their subsequent treatment depends on the fresh determination and any resulting notification.

predicates.appeal_against_case_abatement: A party appeals an order abating pending suits or appeals.
predicates.abatement_based_on_vesting_notification: The abatement order was based on a notification declaring the disputed land vested in the State.
predicates.land_status_unresolved: The land’s qualification as an agricultural area remains to be determined.

issues.definition: When an abatement order is appealed, rests on a vesting notification, and the land’s status remains unresolved, the abatement must be set aside and the cases restored.
